newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns AA minus to Haven Funding stg bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns AA minus to Haven Funding stg bonds.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it assigned its AA minus rating to the 82.5 million stg secured bonds issued by Haven Funding Plc.
(following is a full press release from S&P)
LONDON, March 11 -- Standard & Poor's today has assigned its double-A'-minus rating to the UK82.5 million secured bonds issued by Haven Funding PLC (Haven).
Haven has been established for the limited purpose of issuing bonds and using the net proceeds to fund loans to U.K. housing associations (the "borrowers").
The rating reflects the sound legal analysis of the structure as well as the strong cash flow generating characteristics of the charged portfolio of social housing properties securing each loan.
The quality of each loan's property portfolio, in conjunction with certain structural features of the loans, support debt service capacity over a range of stress scenarios.

The bonds will pay interest semi annually, with amortization of principal beginning in 2017, achieving a repayment of 95% of the bond by 2037 - the remaining 5% is expected to be covered by debt service funds.

Haven's ability to make the scheduled debt payments will depend on it receiving like amounts from the borrowers under their loan agreements. No borrower will have any liability in respect of the obligations of any other borrower and there is no cross collaterization between loans. On financial close, Haven will lend the following amounts to the following housing associations:
Hanover Housing Association UK10.9 million
Kelsey Housing Association Ltd. UK8.2 million
Portsmouth Housing Association Ltd. UK6.9 million
Shaftsbury Housing Association UK22.8 million
Sovereign Housing Association Ltd. UK33.7 million

Each borrower provides a general obligation pledge to its loan. However, each loan has been structured to withstand performance deficiency or insolvency on the part of the borrower through a combination of a fixed charge on identified properties, strong performance covenants, and a minimum 12 months maximum debt service reserve.

The bond trustee is able to enforce the fixed charge security on the occurrence of specific events and appoint a receiver in place of the borrower to collect rents and maintain the charged properties. The loan's debt service reserve has been sized to prevent any interruption in debt payments during this process.
Other important rating factors include:

-- Expected initial overcollaterization of between 1.09 to 1.23 net interest cover for each loan. Each loan's structure is also sufficiently robust to maintain a minimum 1 times debt service coverage over a range of Standard & Poor's stress scenarios.

-- The need for a minimal level of rental inflation with regard to the charged properties. Additionally the current rent levels of each borrower's charged properties fall significantly below market rent levels and the likely housing benefit ceiling, providing reassurance as to the flexibility available to further raise rents.

-- The U.K. housing association environment, which is characterized by strong demand for affordable housing, relatively low arrears and void levels, and an important degree of direct and indirect government support.
-- The individual characteristics of each loan's portfolio of charged property and the potential variability in their future rental income and stock maintenance costs.
-- A general exposure to future housing policy and property market developments, Standard & Poor's said.
